newsitem.title: THAILAND: Talks on new Thai cabinet makeup hit snags.
newsitem.headline: Talks on new Thai cabinet makeup hit snags.

text.p: Thailand's new coalition leader, Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, faced continuing problems with his political partners on Thursday over the makeup of his cabinet, coalition sources said.

Just four days after his New Aspiration Party won the most seats in the general election, Chavalit and leaders of the other five parties in the coalition were still haggling over the allocation of key ministries, the sources said.

They said the main delay stemmed from differences over how to share the economic portfolios. Chavalit has given the economy top priority and has vowed to set up a qualified team capable of improving the nation's slowing economy.
Chavalit favours naming Amnuay Viravan, a respected economist and caretaker foreign minister, as finance minister and deputy premier with control over all economic affairs.
But now questions are being raised as to whether Amnuay, who did not contest Sunday's election, would become even finance minister.
Former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan's Chart Pattana Party (CPP), the second largest coalition member, has insisted on having control over some of the economic ministries.
"Amnuay insists on taking all economic ministries, but our party has people well versed in economic affairs, and they should not be overlooked," a senior CPP source told Reuters.
A close aide of Chavalit said it was possible Amnuay might be left out of the new cabinet.
"At this moment, it's not certain Amnuay will have the sole right to oversee all economic issues, or even be finance minister," he said.

Amnuay had said he must have authority over finance, commerce, industry and foreign affairs to revive Thailand's slowing economy, which is projected to grow six to seven percent this year -- its slowest pace in 10 years.
Amnuay also has said that his nominees should at least be appointed as deputy ministers in these areas.

One of his choices was Ekamol Khiriwat, a former head of the Securities and Exchange Commission who was sacked for alleged leaks of inside information during the previous government of Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa.
Ekamol was fired last December by former finance minister Surakiart Sathirathai, who is tipped as a CPP candidate for foreign minister in Chavalit's cabinet.
